claims.text: Equiatomic FeNiCrMn has a single-phase FCC crystal structure in the proposed initial state.
The proposed FeNiCrMn crystal has a near-zero pre-existing dislocation density.
Shockley partial dislocations nucleate preferentially at pre-existing vacancy clusters or solute-rich hot spots in FeNiCrMn.
Local lattice distortion at vacancy clusters or solute-rich hot spots lowers the dislocation-nucleation barrier.
Dislocation nucleation occurs through cooperative shear of Shockley partials.
The maximum yield stress is significantly higher for loading along <11-1> than along <110>.
The <11-1> loading direction aligns with the primary slip geometry in a way that increases the macroscopic stress required for partial-dislocation emission relative to <110>.
Testing at 10 K suppresses thermal activation sufficiently to isolate the dislocation-nucleation barrier.
FeNiCrMn yield strength is relatively insensitive to strain rate over 10^8–10^10 s^-1.
Vacancy clusters or local chemical inhomogeneities act as nucleation sites for Shockley partial dislocations that generate intrinsic stacking faults.
TiHfZrNb systems exhibit severe local atomic-environment inhomogeneity that creates nucleation hot spots.
Local atomic-environment inhomogeneity raises the dislocation-nucleation energy barrier, permitting large elastic strains to accumulate before nucleation at specific defect sites.
Plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn proceeds through propagation of Shockley partials and formation of intrinsic stacking faults, without twinning or a phase transformation.
The deformed FeNiCrMn sample will not amorphize under the proposed conditions.
The equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi Cantor alloy can form amorphous regions under extreme deformation.
FCC HEA yield strength decreases as temperature increases.
High-stacking-fault-energy systems favor full dislocations or twinning rather than the proposed partial-dislocation mechanism.
In bulk samples, pre-existing dislocations dominate plastic yielding over homogeneous or defect-assisted nucleation barriers.
Pair-distribution-function and diffraction measurements can discriminate an intrinsic stacking fault from a true HCP phase.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says local lattice distortion at vacancy or solute-rich hot spots lowers the nucleation barrier, whereas the mechanism says severe local inhomogeneity raises that barrier.
